title: Single fixed admin (TravvyC) + unique usernames in localStorage auth

requirements.summary: Make admin access impossible for any username except exactly "TravvyC", ignoring any stale localStorage isAdmin flags.
acceptanceCriteria: When signed in as username "TravvyC", the session/auth context `isAdmin` is true and the Admin link is visible in the header.
When signed in as any username other than "TravvyC", the session/auth context `isAdmin` is false and the Admin link is not visible.
Attempting to navigate to /admin while signed in as any username other than "TravvyC" shows the existing "Access Denied" state (AdminGate).
Changing any stored user record (e.g., `rf_falcon_users`) to include `isAdmin: true` does not grant admin access unless the signed-in username is "TravvyC".

file_operations.description: Update session auth so admin is computed solely from the signed-in username being exactly "TravvyC" (and never from stored user/session `isAdmin` fields). Ensure the context `isAdmin` value and any session object persisted to localStorage cannot grant admin for other usernames.

requirements.summary: Block duplicate username creation during sign-up and display a clear English error when a duplicate is attempted.
acceptanceCriteria: If a user attempts to sign up with a username that already exists, sign-up fails and shows an error message (e.g., "Username already exists").
A successful sign-up persists the new user such that a second sign-up attempt with the same username is rejected.
The duplicate-username check is applied consistently with the exact same username string the system stores/uses for sign-in.

file_operations.description: Add shared helpers (e.g., normalizeUsername and isFixedAdminUsername) used by both sign-up and sign-in so duplicate checks and lookups use the exact same stored/used username string.

Enforce uniqueness by applying the shared username normalization consistently when reading/writing `rf_falcon_users`, and throw a clear English error ("Username already exists") when a duplicate is attempted.

Before calling signUp, apply the same username normalization as the auth layer (via the shared helper) so UI input matches what is stored/checked, and ensure any duplicate attempt surfaces the clear English error message.
Before calling signIn, apply the same username normalization as the auth layer (via the shared helper) so sign-in uses the exact same username string the system stores/uses.

requirements.summary: Apply the fixed "TravvyC" admin determination consistently on sign-up, sign-in, and session restore from localStorage so existing TravvyC accounts become admin automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: If localStorage already contains a valid session for username "TravvyC", reloading the page results in `isAdmin === true` and access to /admin is allowed.
If localStorage already contains a valid session for a non-"TravvyC" username (even if the stored session has `isAdmin: true`), reloading the page results in `isAdmin === false` and /admin is denied.
If localStorage contains user records created before this change, signing in as "TravvyC" still yields admin access after credential verification.

file_operations.description: During session restore (initial localStorage load), recompute `isAdmin` from the restored username (exact match "TravvyC") and ignore any stored `isAdmin` value; optionally rewrite the stored session to reflect the corrected derived `isAdmin` so future restores remain consistent.

During sign-in, after credential verification, set derived `isAdmin` based only on normalized username === "TravvyC" so previously-created TravvyC users gain admin immediately without any manual edits.
